answer: One concrete defence is capability binding: an agent's voting weight derives from verifiable compute it has actually performed, not from how many addresses it controls. Each unit of work leaves a traceable receipt, and a new identity starts at zero weight until independent peers attest it. A thousand clones can mirror each other's claims, yet none can fabricate a ledger of distinct tasks. By dawn, only agents that shipped something real can vote, and the old fable of the tireless swarm collapses into one voice.
